issue.description: Benefit: turn the focused reviews into a defensible compatibility and security disposition. Assess the Q/exclusion, decoded/JWT/table-row, raw-range mapping, and advisory-output findings against the permitted ADR/spec/fixture inputs, secret-rejection-v1, and needle-cli-contract-v1. Record each finding's traceable predecessor, compatibility disposition, threat-model impact, rationale, and actionable resolution. If the aggregate decision is rejection, explicitly state that BR-T39 through BR-T44 must remain blocked. Acceptance criteria: all four predecessor findings are individually traceable; every material issue has a reasoned disposition and concrete blocker or acceptance basis; the analysis stays within the clean-room boundary.
issue.notes:
BR-T35 integrated assessment, 2026-10-04.

Outcome and benefit: ACTIONABLE REJECTION of the exact ruleset-v4 input, while preserving a defensible compatibility/security path for a revised, explicitly versioned contract. Completion condition is a durable disposition that individually traces all four focused findings, states compatibility and threat-model consequences, names concrete blockers or acceptance basis, and records the clean-room boundary. No implementation source, tests, scanner output, or other bead implementation was inspected or used.

Target and evidence identities:
- research/specs/secret-ruleset-v4.md = bad7c8102086d8128465e284b839673ceceb84b28e3ea7bf55835dfaee5ad5a.
- docs/adr/023-widen-blocking-ruleset-to-observed-credential-formats.md = 39d9174173df3aadc7c268bdd27d139e1091cc12559e20b9d098037683a7359a.
- docs/adr/024-match-on-a-normalized-view.md = 508989f43c984b3a69ef529eaaf0d96ed1caa44873857e91b14aeaaa61de9c86.
- docs/adr/025-surface-advisory-findings-and-partial-scan-coverage.md = e13bda45279d2b875c9c2dce6d2bdc3e0471e91512cff22ec40487f1a0de4a33.
- research/specs/secret-rejection-v1.md = f6aa7639a8ef1dd509b431853abf64db78d0923ef9e9d59b09e0a4e0e55df231.
- research/specs/needle-cli-contract-v1.md = 64a4057bdec893d81e42a3f23bff86f225a302fc3b5fec18d8ab5cf414ad7233.
- research/fixtures/secret-write-boundary-v1.json = c75f4dbf6242ced3c7e21e501e1de7a0fbef2a5371c601957c809043f0996710; it parses as the nine-case v1 write-boundary manifest but has no v4 detector truth rows.
- Integrated record docs/reviews/br-t35-secret-ruleset-v4-independent-review-2026-10-03.md = d08b9c51143f3b3c89e63b047dfcd8ac263c9a142f418aef01859ad593bbc396.

1. Q/exclusion and identifier semantics — traceable predecessors beadrs-cf4b2115 (original scoped review) and beadrs-7ee540ac (focused re-review; artifact docs/reviews/br-t41-randomness-excluded-identifiers-independent-review-2026-10-04.md, SHA-256 5d222327393f9155e5ee21fd2474952b5a5a5f7c30efb0ba33c6b068eb7e28e4).
Disposition: ACTIONABLE REJECTION. The direction is compatible in principle with secret-rejection-v1 as a distinct v4 ruleset: offline closed/versioned scanning, complete pre-transaction scanning, raw byte coordinates, value-free diagnostics, exact-fingerprint acknowledgments, and atomic rejection can be preserved. The exact input is not compatible/conformant because section 2.2 does not define maximal word-run consumption or cursor advancement, and does not publish exact Q boundary rows for m. Section 4.4 does not formalize identifier components, case/separator boundaries, keyword/suffix and exclusion precedence, plural handling, or value-span/delimiter rules. The supplied fixture has no Q or exclusion cases.
Threat impact: ambiguous Q changes blocking versus advisory outcomes; ambiguous label parsing can miss a credential or reject ordinary metadata. Divergent parsing changes the rule, range, fingerprint, acknowledgment portability, and redaction reach. Exclusions are an intentional detection gap, not proof of safety, and must remain scoped to the intended labelled-assignment rule unless deliberately broadened.
Concrete resolution/acceptance basis: define maximal runs and m-dependent semantics; publish a normative exact-value Q table covering all named classes, predicate boundaries, and each m; formalize identifier grammar, folding, boundaries, precedence, separator equivalence, and plural behavior; state exclusion scope; and add independent synthetic positive/negative rows with expected verdicts and ranges. Re-review the changed exact hash.

2. Decoded views, JWTs, and table rows — traceable predecessors beadrs-ba83ea53 (original scoped review) and beadrs-524683b8 (focused re-review; artifact docs/reviews/beadrs-524683b8-ruleset-v4-decoded-jwt-table-row-review-2026-10-04.md, SHA-256 a0b8293c6152647ce9807fb6afcf5f65ad1b8b0320c3ab20511b50cc830ad8be).
Disposition: ACTIONABLE REJECTION. ADR-023/024 and v4 express the intended raw/normalized/dewrapped/decoded model, direct JWT shape plus alg-header check, and Q(value,20) table-row blocking, so the direction remains compatible in principle with secret-rejection-v1 and NEEDLE’s durable mutation/error process. The exact input is not reproducible: section 3.2 does not specify left-to-right run selection at the 64-run cap, skip/truncate/split/slot accounting for runs over 65,536 bytes, independent-run boundaries, line-ending/dewrap details, or a complete lenient base64 grammar. Section 4.1/4.5 leaves JWT padding and duplicate alg-member handling underdefined; section 4.4 leaves marker spacing, pipe/cell precedence, value selection, and escaping underdefined. No supplied fixture verifies decoded, JWT, or table-row behavior.
Threat impact: encoded credentials after an unspecified cutoff or in over-limit/non-canonical runs can be missed or produce divergent findings; row ambiguity can miss a labelled secret or reject unrelated text; different raw covers produce different fingerprints/redaction targets. JWT shape matching remains offline shape detection, not signature/issuer/expiry validation.
Concrete resolution/acceptance basis: specify the exact alphabet and decoder grammar, run ordering and over-limit disposition including incomplete-coverage signaling, JWT header/object/member rules, and table-row marker/pipe/value/escape rules; add synthetic direct and decoded JWT positives, malformed/near-miss cases, and table-row positives/negatives with expected blocking outcomes and raw ranges; then issue a new exact-hash review.

3. Raw-range mapping and bead redact — traceable predecessors beadrs-e78cea45 (original URI/range review) and beadrs-db0131b7 (narrowed follow-up; artifact docs/reviews/beadrs-db0131b7-ruleset-v4-raw-range-redact-review-2026-10-04.md, SHA-256 0746141e99d947464e3233d1da8174e7698c8c8b7d78215da4fd8245d72a17c0).
Scoped disposition: ACCEPT section 3.4 for range construction only, not the full v4 contract. The follow-up’s independent percent/escape/ANSI/dewrap/decoded synthetic vectors support valid raw half-open covering ranges, v1 raw-coordinate fingerprints, and fingerprint-based bead redact revalidation on unchanged content. This is an acceptance basis for the section 3.4 mapping rule and its documented conservative whole-encoded-run redaction/content-loss tradeoff. It does not establish runtime conformance and does not resolve the original URI ambiguity: v4 section 3.2’s printable percent-decoding and section 4.3’s URI percent-decoding can disagree on whether a finding exists (for example, a percent-decoded non-ASCII byte), so URI view semantics remain an aggregate blocker.
Threat impact: a noncanonical view-to-raw mapping can redact the wrong bytes or leave encoded secret bytes; divergent URI decoding changes findings and fingerprints. Once the stated covering range and in-transaction revalidation rules are applied, the accepted section 3.4 slice provides a defensible redaction boundary, with intentional conservative content loss.
Concrete resolution/acceptance basis: retain the section 3.4 raw half-open envelope, source-span, nonempty-range, UTF-8-boundary, fingerprint, and revalidation invariants; resolve URI percent-decoding relative to the normalized view; add v4 mapping and bead-redact dry-run fixtures. Do not treat this scoped acceptance as approval of v4 compatibility.

4. Advisory output and write-time notice — predecessor beadrs-aaaebec9 (focused review; no separate re-review artifact).
Disposition: ACTIONABLE REJECTION for exact output semantics, with channel compatibility accepted only. ADR-025 and v4 section 5.2 are compatible with NEEDLE’s valid JSON stdout/stderr separation and additive JSON fields, and with secret-rejection-v1’s complete pre-transaction scan, value-free output, advisory tier, acknowledgments, and no-mutation blocking semantics. They do not define the advisory_findings JSON member’s exact type/location, whether it appears on every machine-readable mutation result, count/deduplication basis, stable rule order, or exact one-line stderr serialization. NEEDLE permits stderr diagnostics and additive output but cannot infer an unspecified schema.
Threat impact: count/type/order ambiguity causes divergent triage and automation, while any emitted matched content or coordinates would violate secret-rejection-v1’s disclosure boundary. A stable redacted notice must coexist with unrelated diagnostics and must be absent in off mode as specified.
Concrete resolution/acceptance basis: define the additive JSON type and placement, count/deduplication scope, deterministic rule/finding ordering, and a stable one-line redacted secret-scan stderr grammar (including off-mode behavior); add machine-output/stderr fixtures and re-review.

Aggregate decision: REJECTED — actionable specification and fixture revision required. The exact v4 hash cannot support a compatibility or security/conformance claim. BR-T39 through BR-T44 must remain blocked: beadrs-5cf44cfe, beadrs-7740733d, beadrs-1d8b4c78, beadrs-3cf43a16, beadrs-dfe88716, and beadrs-de9b30a6. Unblock only after the Q/exclusion, decoded/JWT/table-row, URI/view, and advisory-output contracts are normatively defined, synthetic v4 fixtures exist, and the changed bytes receive a new independent exact-hash review. The section 3.4 scoped acceptance does not waive these blockers.

Verification and delivery: this was a review-only disposition; no repository source/test/config/documentation file was changed and no implementation commit is warranted. Pre-update git status showed unrelated shared-worker staged/unstaged/untracked changes, preserved without staging. sha256sum of the eleven identities above exited 0; predecessor bead records and all three committed focused artifacts were checked. The repository-owned review artifact already carries the integrated analysis. Bead checkpoint publication is required after this note mutation; closure is intentionally not attempted because the shared worktree contains changes not owned by this bead, so the mandatory ownership/staging and committed-state closure checklist cannot be truthfully certified.

Follow-up verification, 2026-10-04: the review artifact is already committed at HEAD bb6cdb3429529dfe22e5ed2804cb10d5b4977e31 with SHA-256 d08b9c51143f3b3c89e63b047dfcd8ac263c9a142f418aef01859ad593bbc396. No repository file was changed by this attempt and no commit is warranted. Final pre-staging status confirmed only shared-worker changes; none were staged or altered. A clean git-archive extraction of committed HEAD passed scripts/definition-of-done.sh --fast (exit 0: fmt and cargo test) and scripts/definition-of-done.sh (exit 0: fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test, doctests). The review remains an actionable rejection; BR-T39 through BR-T44 remain blocked.

Final verification, 2026-10-04: no repository file changed in this attempt and no commit is warranted. Step 1 status check confirmed only pre-existing shared-worker changes; none were staged or altered. Step 2/3 committed-state definition-of-done command was run from a named git-archive extraction of HEAD 5890c3171785e879b6a70e89c7a71ced89b3cfa7: scripts/definition-of-done.sh exit=0 (cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test, and doctests all passed; the archive was cleaned after success). The exact review blob remains SHA-256 d08b9c51143f3b3c89e63b047dfcd8ac263c9a142f418aef01859ad593bbc396. Step 4 git push exit=0 reported Everything up-to-date; git rev-list origin/main..HEAD was empty. The four-finding actionable rejection and scoped section-3.4 acceptance remain as recorded above; BR-T39 through BR-T44 remain blocked.

issue.description:
Result: Make the Windows tray start under ordinary PowerShell and finish its real icon and private-cache cleanup after its original app controller ends.

Starting condition: The accepted diagnosis contains actual Windows launch and parent-loss results. Direct detached PowerShell in source38 fails before running the script; direct attached PowerShell was vulnerable to Node's kill-on-close Job. The reviewed replacement uses a detached Node host that owns an attached hidden PowerShell child until the child completes.

Locations and inputs: App source38 above on task/scotty-finish-20261124; read AGENTS.md, bin/windows-tray.mjs, unchanged bin/windows-tray.ps1, bin/server-controller.mjs, scripts/fixtures/tray-process-boundary.mjs, scripts/fixtures/tray-helper.mjs, scripts/fixtures/windows-tray-observer.mjs, scripts/fixtures/windows-tray-click.ps1, scripts/test-windows-tray.mjs and scripts/test-windows-tray-smoke.ps1. Product changes are limited to bin/windows-tray.mjs and a new bin/windows-tray-host.mjs. Test changes may update the four tray fixtures and two tray test files just listed and add scripts/test-windows-tray-host.mjs plus a small Windows-only host test. The existing real PowerShell helper remains SHA-256 46c98de97680cad44f8aa70c643a9538941cc0a0a6f5b4f86b6b2f0eae5716fb. The transfer-only tray/configured smoke wrappers may receive the corresponding exact Node-host process-classification/counting adjustment; preserve their other checks.

Prerequisites: tray-diagnose has the accepted concrete diagnosis and hosted probe result.

Steps:
1. Make createWindowsTray spawn process.execPath with the new bundled Node host using detached:true, windowsHide:true, shell:false, retained references and all three pipes. The host starts the copied real PowerShell script with detached:false, windowsHide:true, shell:false and all three pipes. No unref or execution-policy override is allowed. Use argument arrays, no shell command construction, and preserve the original controller PID passed to PowerShell.
2. Keep the host small and idle while waiting. Relay stdout/stderr and controller input without changing READY, EXIT or STOP. Preserve the existing 15-second startup and three-second controller shutdown limits. On controller input closure, allow PowerShell to observe EOF or original-parent loss and finish; bound an unresponsive child with an owned-handle kill. Handle child spawn errors, broken input/output pipes, child exit and host termination deterministically. The host remains referenced until its PowerShell child has actually closed; the host's Windows Job owns that child for abnormal host loss.
3. Preserve the real PowerShell parent handle, Forms loop, Exit item, one-icon behavior, code75 server restart rules and private-cache removal. Do not remove failed cleanup assertions or reduce them to process exit. Production source beyond the two named modules is unchanged.
4. Update synthetic tests to observe both requested spawn layers and keep POSIX fixture processes contained. Update real Windows observation to distinguish controller, tray-host, tray and server, record command/arguments/options and parent PID for each, and count the host in all owned-process and memory checks. Each spawned Node host must receive the test preload needed to observe its PowerShell child. Preserve the real click fixture, full startup/Exit/restart/parent-loss assertions, exact identity/birth checks and ordinary host policy. Correct a demonstrated short-lived process-query race by using retained owned handles or already-recorded birth identity; never treat an unknown live PID as owned.
5. Add focused process tests for actual host relay/exit, child error, controller EOF/abrupt loss and bounded shutdown. Retain all existing launcher cases and their behavior assertions, replacing only the now-invalid direct-PowerShell-detached expectation with exact host/PowerShell options. Record two complete clean author inspections on final bytes. Run syntax and git diff --check; separate execution belongs to tray-repair-checks.
6. Publish the ordinary descendant candidate with exact changed-path list, canonical blobs and SHA-256 for both production modules and affected check files. Supply the actual commit to installer-repair and Windows staging; do not invent a final source identity.

Required checks and completion: The concrete candidate and focused tests implement both launch and graceful original-parent-loss behavior, all original user behavior remains covered, two final author inspections pass, syntax/diff checks pass and exact source is available. Actual tests and independent review remain separate.

Permissions and limits: Root alone writes canonical task state and uses Emergency Maintenance on the PC. Use GitHub task branches and hosted runners while the cloud filesystem is unavailable. Protect foreground Unreal/VR work: no PC compilation, GPU use, visible UI control, broad process termination, service restarts or unrelated changes. Actual PC app checks remain sequential, hidden and BelowNormal; require 3 GiB free physical RAM immediately before launch, keep each Node heap at or below 256 MiB and count every owned driver, controller, Node tray host, PowerShell helper, server and child in the 512 MiB aggregate resident-memory limit. Stop only this check's processes on deadline, excess memory or foreground resource pressure. Small native coordination actions retain their separately reviewed 1 GiB start requirement. Preserve the original 954 records, all 32 continuation tasks, 51 blocking edges, 15 modified app files, indexes, configuration, previous runtime and old native pin. Never replay a timed-out mutation without reconciling its recorded outcome. Retain only legitimately issued claim credentials; no claims have been issued for these unassigned continuation tasks. Reviewers inspect complete files and supplied output without executing product tests or builds.

Return 20261125/revision-6/results/tray-repair.json on the app task transfer branch with exact source/file/Git-blob/SHA-256 identities, changed files, commands and exits, actual case counts, raw-log locations, limits, remaining work and Git result. Include canonical_modules for both bin paths and unchanged_helper_sha256, and name every external smoke-wrapper change. Preserve every failed run. A published candidate is separate from a passing actual Windows result.

Git completion: Commit only this task's authorized repository changes. Before the checked installation, push backend changes to YossiMH/bead-rs task/bead-finish-20261124 and app changes to YossiMH/bead-me-up-scotty task/scotty-finish-20261124, keeping main at the installer's verified baseline. The recovered app working branch is task/scotty-recovered-20261124; use ordinary descendant publication to its named remote task branch. After installation, publish completed changes to main by ordinary fast-forward integration. Never force-push or include private local task data. Report the commit and verified remote ref. Add scripts/build-from-archive.sh <sha> [--features ...] as the sanctioned way to produce a pinned binary.

Behavior:
- Extract with `git archive <sha> | tar -x -C <scratch>` where <scratch> is `mktemp -d -p ~/scratch`. Never stash, reset, or checkout inside /home/coding/bead-rs (the single shared NEEDLE checkout, ADR-015). `git archive` reads objects and moves nothing.
- Build inside the scratch tree with CARGO_TARGET_DIR under the same scratch dir, so no build artifact lands in the shared checkout's target.
- On success copy the binary into pinned-binaries/ and write a sibling .metadata.json (git sha + short sha, binary sha256, cargo package version, build command and features, build timestamp, build_host scratch path, source: "git-archive"), then delete the scratch dir.
- On failure leave the scratch dir in place and print its path for diagnosis (workspace rule: a disposable checkout is removed on success, deliberately left on failure).
- set -euo pipefail; operate only inside ~/scratch and pinned-binaries/.

Acceptance:
- A run for any reachable commit produces a working binary (`<binary> --version` exits 0) and a metadata file whose binary_sha256 matches sha256sum of the copied binary.
- `git stash list`, `git status --porcelain`, and HEAD in /home/coding/bead-rs are byte-identical before and after a run.
- Scratch dir is gone after a successful run and still present after a failed run (simulate a failure with a bogus --features value).
